title.en: The War of Resistance Against Japan

description.zh:
1931 年九一八事变至 1945 年日本签署投降书，中国人民进行了长达十四年的抗日战争。本专题以日军进攻、中国各抗日部队与盟军为主线，分设国民党军正面战场、集团军、八路军、新四军、华南游击队、中国政府、中国民众、国际组织与多边会议等实体，分别呈现正面战场部队序列、华北华中敌后根据地与政治外交事件，呈现从东北沦陷、全面抗战爆发、战略相持到最终胜利的时空脉络。

> 部分战役路线（淞沪、平型关、忻口、台儿庄、兰封、随枣、昆仑关、南京、武汉、长沙（第一、二、三次会战）、枣宜、上高、中条山、鄂西、常德、衡阳、湘西、滇西、百团、远征军/缅北、豫湘桂）据常见战史地图整理；其余路线为示意简化。2026-11-16 起按 C5—C7 端点核查计划分批核对线头线尾：日军进攻线 21 处已补灵丘、大同、青岛、菏泽、开封、商城、芜湖、归绥、舞阳、当阳、郑州、深圳、曼德勒、杭州、安阳、荆州、公安、邵阳等出兵或占领节点，一·二八段改为虹口—闸北，兰封段改为菏泽—兰封—开封，六安段改为六安—商城；中国军队的忻口、平型关、昆仑关、百团大战、上高、中条山、鄂西、滇西等 12 处与盟军/华南 6 处也已核对：忻口段改为南怀化—大白水战场线，百团大战西端校正至榆次并补正太路破袭事件，昆仑关段补第 5 军自柳州反攻，滇西反攻补保山强渡怒江与攻克畹町两端；华南游击队三条活动区尾端按示意线登记。2026-11-19 补录 1932—1936 年事件 26 条（锦州沦陷、榆关抗战、热河作战、长城抗战、察哈尔民众抗日同盟军、塘沽协定、何梅协定、秦土协定、绥远抗战等）与 12 另设「国际组织与多边会议」，把李顿调查团、国联大会通过报告书与九国公约会议从中国政府层移出，并补 1931 年中国向国联申诉事件。2026-11-20 梳理八路军层：事件由 11 条增至 29 条，补雁门关、阳明堡、七亘村、神头岭、响堂铺、长乐村、齐会、黄土岭、关家垴、狼牙山、韩略村、南下支队与 1945 年大反攻，路线由 9 段增至 24 段。2026-11-20 description.en:
From the Mukden Incident in September 1931 to Japan’s formal surrender in September 1945, China fought a fourteen-year war of resistance. This atlas follows the Japanese advance, China’s resistance forces, and the Allied forces, with separate layers for the KMT frontline forces, group armies, the Eighth Route Army, the New Fourth Army, South China guerrillas, the Chinese government, the Chinese people, and international organizations and multilateral conferences. It covers the frontline order of battle, the anti-Japanese base areas in North and Central China, and political and diplomatic events, from the fall of the Northeast and the outbreak of full-scale war to protracted resistance and final victory.

> Selected campaign routes (Shanghai, Pingxingguan, Xinkou, Taierzhuang, Lanfeng, Suizao, Kunlun Pass, Nanjing, Wuhan, Changsha (first, second, and third battles), Zaoyang–Yichang, Shanggao, South Shanxi, West Hubei, Changde, Hengyang, West Hunan, Western Yunnan, Hundred Regiments, the Expeditionary Force/Northern Burma, and Henan-Hunan-Guangxi) follow common historical maps; other routes remain simplified. From 16 November 2026 the C5–C7 endpoint review checks heads and tails in batches: the 21 Japanese advance endpoints now carry documented departure or capture nodes (Lingqiu, Datong, Qingdao, Heze, Kaifeng, Shangcheng, Wuhu, Guisui, Wuyang, Dangyang, Zhengzhou, Shenzhen, Mandalay, Hangzhou, Anyang, Jingzhou, Gong’an, Shaoyang), the January 28 leg becomes Hongkou–Zhabei, Lanfeng becomes Heze–Lanfeng–Kaifeng and Lu’an becomes Lu’an–Shangcheng; the 12 Chinese and 6 Allied/South China endpoints have also been checked: the Xinkou leg now follows the Nanhuaihua–Dabaishui battle line, the Hundred Regiments line is corrected to Yuci with a documented railway-sabotage event, Kunlun Pass gains the 5th Corps’ departure from Liuzhou, and the western Yunnan counter-offensive is anchored at the Salween crossing and Wanding; the three South China guerrilla area tails are registered as schematic activity zones. On 19 November 2026, 26 events and 12 route segments were added for 1932–1936 (the fall of Jinzhou, the defense of Shanhaiguan, the Rehe campaign, the Great Wall campaign, the Chahar People’s Anti-Japanese Allied Army, the Tanggu Truce, the He-Umezu and Qin-Doihara agreements, and the Suiyuan campaign), filling the gap between the establishment of Manchukuo and the December Ninth Movement. From 19 November 2026 the “Chinese resistance” narrative chain was split by participating units, and the mixed layer was further divided into “Chinese Government” and “Chinese People”: ten cross-theater connector segments (including Yangquan–Kunming) were removed, military routes were reassigned to the KMT frontline, group-army, Eighth Route Army, and Allied layers, and unit histories were added for the 74th, 5th, 10th, and 18th Armies and the 33rd Group Army. On 19 November 2026 a separate “International Organizations and Multilateral Conferences” layer was added: the Lytton Commission, the League Assembly’s adoption of its report, and the Nine-Power Conference were moved out of the Chinese government layer, and China’s 1931 appeal to the League was added. On 20 November 2026 the Eighth Route Army layer was expanded from 11 to 29 events, adding Yanmenguan, Yangmingbao, Qigencun, Shentouling, Xiangtangpu, Changlecun, Qihui, Huangtuling, Guanjianao, Langya Mountain, Hanluecun, the Southward Column, and the 1945 general counter-offensive, with routes increased from 9 to 24 segments. On 20 November 2026 three strategic turning points were added: the Luochuan Conference, which set “independent mountain guerrilla warfare”; the Shiguan Conference after the fall of Taiyuan, which dispersed the three divisions behind enemy lines; and the April 1938 directive on plains guerrilla warfare, followed by the 129th Division’s advance into southern Hebei. Events rose from 366 to 370 and routes from 238 to 241. On 20 November 2026 the entry of the 115th Division’s main force into Shandong (March 1939) was added, together with a note that the Shandong Column was formed from local uprising forces; events rose from 370 to 371 and routes from 241 to 242. From 20 November 2026 the Japanese layer was systematically expanded by actor: Changchun, Jilin, Qiqihar and the Japan–Manchukuo Protocol in the Northeast; Beiping, Tianjin, Zhangjiakou, Baoding, Shijiazhuang, Niangziguan, Guisui, Baotou, Jinan, Hangzhou, the Jinshanwei landing, the provisional and reformed puppet governments, the Kōain, Hirota’s Three Principles, the two Konoe statements, the North/Central China development companies and the Trautmann mediation in North China; Xiamen, Shantou, Chaozhou, Bao’an, Nanning, Hong Kong, the Shanghai Settlement, the Leizhou Peninsula and Guangzhouwan in South China; Nanchang, Anqing, Jiujiang, Xuzhou, Yichang, Ningbo–Shaoxing, the three falls of Wenzhou and the two falls of Fuzhou in Central China; the coastal blockade, the Chengdu bombing, the Ningbo/Changde/Zhejiang–Jiangxi bacteriological attacks and the Pingdingshan/Panjiayu/Beituan/Changjiao massacres at the strategic level; and the invasion of western Yunnan, Quzhou/Shangrao, the falls of Zhengzhou, Xuchang, Luoyang, Changsha, Hengyang, Guilin, Liuzhou and Dushan, the Hunan–Guangdong–Jiangxi border operation at Shaoguan/Nanxiong/Dayu/Ganzhou/Suichuan airfield, Laohekou and the retrocession of Taiwan in 1942–1945. Japanese events rose from 128 to 281 and routes from 64 to 124; the atlas rose from 377 to 529 events and from 243 to 303 routes. On 20 November 2026, M204 added Japanese actions in Hainan: the Tiandu iron mine, the Shilu–Basuo railway, the Yulin–Beili railway, the Tiandu mass grave, the first occupation, the 1942 “sweep” and the 1945 surrender, with the Tiandu–Yulin and Yulin–Beili supply routes; the atlas rose from 461 to 468 events and from 268 to 270 routes. On 20 November 2026, M205 further added the extent of the occupation: the falls of Yacheng, Ding’an, Wenchang, Chengmai, Jiaji, Lingao, Dan county, Lingshui, Tunchang, Gan’en, Changjiang, Wanning, Baoting and Ledong, together with an overview of the occupied county towns and garrisons by March 1940; Japan occupied the county towns and most market towns of 14 counties, established more than 360 posts and 195 maintenance associations, while Baisha county town and the Wuzhishan mountains were not permanently occupied. Japanese events rose from 220 to 235 and the atlas from 468 to 483 events, with routes unchanged. On 20 November 2026, M206 added Hainan landing points and departure points: Chengmai Bay/Laocheng, Yazhou Bay at Touzao/Dadan/Maling, Baimajing, Qinglan port and Basuo/Beili, with thirteen advance routes (Laocheng–Jinjiang, Baimajing–Xinying–Xinzhou, Touzao–Yacheng, Haikou–Ding’an, Haikou–Wenchang–Qinglan, Sanya–Tengqiao–Lingshui, Wenchang–Jiaji, Jinjiang–Lingao, Jiaji–Wanning, Lingshui–Baoting, Yacheng–Ledong, Basuo–Shilu and Basuo–Duntou–Xinjie); Japanese events rose from 235 to 240, routes from 91 to 104, and the atlas from 483 to 488 events and from 270 to 283 routes. The departure points for Tunchang, Gan’en and Jiaji remain uncertain and are not drawn as routes. On 20 November 2026, M207 refined the Guangdong front: the first occupation of Sanzao Island, the Liantang Bay landing and the Sanzao massacre; the three Dayawan landings at Pinghai/Renshan, Yanzaobei and Aotou/Xiachong; Danshui, Huizhou, Boluo, Zengcheng, Conghua and Humen; Sanshui, Foshan, Shunde, Panyu, Jiangmen, Xinhui, Zhongshan and the Tangjia/Xiangzhou landing; the first and third falls of Bao’an; Nan’ao and Chenghai; and the Guangzhou and Shantou surrenders, with fifteen routes. Japanese events rose from 240 to 267 and routes from 104 to 119; the atlas rose from 488 to 515 events and from 283 to 298 routes. On 20 November 2026, M208 added the northern Guangdong campaign nodes: Xiaolou/Zhengguo, Yonghan, Conghua, Liangkou, Meikeng/Lü tian, Xinfeng, Wengyuan, Yingde and Xinjiang in the first campaign; Hua county, Jiekou, Jilonggang, Liangkou and Shiliuhuading in the second; with five routes including Guangzhou–Hua county–Yinzhan’ao–Yuantan–Yingde. Japanese events rose from 267 to 281 and routes from 119 to 129; the atlas rose from 515 to 529 events and from 298 to 308 routes. Dates and coordinates still await historical review. From 20 November 2026 the atlas supports regional browsing: 426 historical administrative units/places and region assignments for all 529 events and 308 routes, filterable by province/municipality, county/city, or place. Cross-province routes stay whole and are labelled at both ends when zoomed in. The historical provincial outlines are four hand-drawn schematic snapshots (1931, 1937, 1938–1944, 1945), not survey-grade; county boundaries are not drawn because no redistributable Republican-era county geometry is available. On 21 November 2026, M213 refined the Jiangsu front. In southern Jiangsu it added the first Japanese air raid on Suzhou, the Baimaokou landing, Kunshan, Changshu, Suzhou, Wuxi, Yixing, Changzhou, the Jiangyin fortress, Danyang, Jintan, Liyang, Lishui, Jurong, Zhenjiang and Yangzhou, together with the Xuxiang and Wanfu Bridge massacres; in northern Jiangsu it added the Yaogang landing at Nantong, Rugao, Haimen, Dongtai, Yancheng, Funing, Suqian, Lianyungang, Haizhou, Huaiyin, Gaoyou and Taizhou, plus the Fourth Sub-district clearance campaign. It added 31 events and 20 routes (#130–#149). Japanese events rose from 281 to 312 and routes from 129 to 149; the atlas rose from 529 to 560 events and from 308 to 328 routes. All routes are schematic; variant dates and sources are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-jiangsu.md. On 21 November 2026, M214 refined the Anhui front: 38 events covering Guangde, Langxi, Xuancheng, Wuhu, Dangtu, the Ma'anshan mines, Quanjiao, Chuxian, Mingguang, Chihe, Linhuaiguan, Dingyuan, Fengyang, Bengbu, Huaiyuan, Mengcheng, Xiaoxian, Suxian, Dangshan, Guoyang, Boxian, Hefei, Qianshan, Taihu, Susong, Lu'an, Huoshan, Dongliu, Guichi and Tongling, plus the Panay incident, the Shanmacun massacre, the Huainan coal mines, the puppet Anhui provincial government, the southern Anhui and Chaoxian–Wuwei sweeps, the Lingbi–Wuhe massacre and the Bengbu surrender, with 18 routes (#150–#167). Japanese events rose from 312 to 350 and routes from 149 to 167; the atlas rose from 560 to 598 events and from 328 to 346 routes; Anhui Japanese events rose from 5 to 43. All routes are schematic; variant dates and sources are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-anhui.md. On 21 November 2026, M215 refined the Shandong front: 31 events covering Dezhou, Linqing, Gaotang, Zhoucun, Zichuan, Tai'an, Qingdao, Weixian, Yanzhou, Qufu, Zouxian, Jining, Sishui, Wenshang, Jimo, Yantai, Huangxian, Weihaiwei, Tengxian, Lincheng, Yixian, Zaozhuang, Linyi, Yuncheng, Jinxiang and Liaocheng, plus the puppet Shandong government, the fall of Rongcheng, the Yimeng Mountains "iron wall" sweep, the defence of Ma'anshan and the Jinan–Qingdao–Dezhou surrender, with 18 routes (#168–#185). Japanese events rose from 350 to 381 and routes from 167 to 185; the atlas rose from 598 to 629 events and from 346 to 364 routes; Shandong Japanese events rose from 6 to 36 (plus one under Qingdao municipality). All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-shandong.md. On 21 November 2026, M216 refined the Zhejiang front with 25 events covering Jiaxing, Huzhou, Changxing, the Qiaosi massacre, the Wuchaomiao massacre in Fuyang, the Longxi massacre, Xiaoshan, Zhenhai (1940), Cixi, Fenghua, Yuyao, the Dajiao massacre, the Maoyang fluorite mine in Xiangshan, Zhuji, Dongyang, Yiwu, Jinhua, Lanxi, Lishui, Shengxian, Xinchang, the second fall of Lishui, the puppet Zhejiang government, the Fuyang surrender talks and the disarmament of Japanese troops in Hangzhou, with 16 routes (#186–#201). Existing events for Hangzhou, the Ningbo bacteriological attack, Shaoxing, the 1941 fall of Zhenhai, Ruian, the two falls of Wenzhou, Ningbo, the Zhejiang–Jiangxi campaign and Quzhou were not duplicated. Japanese events rose from 381 to 406 and routes from 185 to 201; the atlas rose from 629 to 654 events and from 364 to 380 routes; Zhejiang Japanese events rose from 14 to 39. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-zhejiang.md. On 21 November 2026, M217 refined the Fujian front with 11 events covering the Liaoluo Bay landing and fall of Kinmen, the Xiamen naval engagement, the falls of Changle and Lianjiang, the Dongshan port landing and defence, the second Japanese–puppet attack on Dongshan, the Yongning and Chongwu massacres, and the Xiamen surrender, with 5 routes (#202–#206). Existing events for the Xiamen landing and fall, the two Min River landings and the two falls of Fuzhou were not duplicated. Japanese events rose from 406 to 417 and routes from 201 to 206; the atlas rose from 654 to 665 events and from 380 to 385 routes; Fujian Japanese events rose from 6 to 17. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-fujian.md. On 21 November 2026, M218 refined the Jiangxi front with 10 events covering the fall of the Madang fortress, Pengze, Hukou, Xingzi, Ruichang, De'an, Yongxiu, Gao'an, Fengxin and Nankang, with 9 routes (#207–#215). Existing events for Jiujiang, Nanchang, Shangrao, Ganzhou, Dayu and the Suichuan airfield were not duplicated. Japanese events rose from 417 to 427 and routes from 206 to 215; the atlas rose from 665 to 675 events and from 385 to 394 routes; Jiangxi Japanese events rose from 11 to 21. This completes Stage 1, the six provinces of East China (Jiangsu, Anhui, Shandong, Zhejiang, Fujian and Jiangxi). All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-jiangxi.md. On 21 November 2026, M219 refined the Hebei front with 10 events covering Langfang, Tongzhou, Cangzhou, Dingxian, Xingtai, Handan, Cixian and Daming, plus the Beiping and Tianjin surrenders, with 6 routes (#216–#221). Existing events for Beiping, Tianjin, Baoding, Shijiazhuang, Nankou, Lugouqiao, Panjiayu, the May 1942 sweep and Beituan were not duplicated. Japanese events rose from 427 to 437 and routes from 215 to 221; the atlas rose from 675 to 685 events and from 394 to 400 routes; Hebei-related Japanese events (including the Beiping and Tianjin municipalities) rose from 17 to 27. County dates that lacked two independent sources were not hard-recorded; all routes are schematic. Sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-hebei.md. On 21 November 2026, M221 refined the Henan front: 46 events covering Anyang, Nanle, Qingfeng, Puyang, Tangyin, Qi County, Changyuan, Fengqiu, Jixian, Xinxiang, Huojia, Jiaozuo, Jiyuan, Yongcheng, Shangqiu, Qi County (Qixian), Tongxu, Weishi, Zhongmou, Gushi, Huangchuan, Guangshan, Luoshan, Xinyang, Queshan, Zhumadian, Biyang, Xinzheng, Changge, Linying, Luohe, Xiping, Yu County, Jiaxian, Linru, Dengfeng, Lushan, Gong County, Mianchi, Xin’an, Nanyang, Xixiakou and Xichuan, plus the Zhengzhou and Luohe surrenders, with 18 routes (#234–#251). Japanese events rose from 458 to 504 and routes from 233 to 251; the atlas rose from 706 to 752 events and from 412 to 430 routes; Henan Japanese events rose from 17 to 63. The 1938 northern Henan axis and the 1944 central Henan axis are drawn separately, not merged into one line. Huixian, Xiuwu, Bo’ai, Qinyang, Mengxian, Taikang, Chenliu, Zhengyang, Runan, Mi County, Yanshi, Yancheng, Suiping, Xiangcheng, Baofeng, Lingbao, Wenxiang and Song County lacked two independent sources or had conflicting dates, so they were not hard-recorded. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-henan.md. On 21 November 2026, M222 refined the Suiyuan and Chahar fronts: 15 events covering the Chahar Detachment headquarters at Dolon, the Battle of Zhangbei, Wanquan, Dushikou, Huailai, Yanqing, Chicheng, Xuanhua, Chaigoubu, Yu County, Fengzhen, Xinghe, Jining, Liangcheng and Salaqi, with 7 routes (#252–#258); the existing #89 “Datong–Guisui–Baotou” was refined to run through Fengzhen, Jining, Zhuozi, Guisui, Salaqi and Baotou. Japanese events rose from 504 to 519 and routes from 251 to 258; the atlas rose from 752 to 767 events and from 430 to 437 routes; Suiyuan/Chahar Japanese events rose from 13 to 28. Zhangbei had been under Japanese control since the 1935 Qin-Doihara agreement, so the entry records a Japanese sortie from Zhangbei, not a “fall of Zhangbei”; the northern, eastern and southern Chahar axes and the southern and northern Suiyuan axes are drawn separately. The December 1935 occupation of eight Chahar counties, Taolin/Bailingmiao in September 1937, Huai’an, Yangyuan, Longguan, Togtoh, Guyang, Qingshuihe, Horinger and Wuchuan lacked two independent sources or had conflicting dates, so they were not hard-recorded. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-suiyuan-chahar.md. On 21 November 2026, M223 refined the Hubei front: 36 events covering 21 from the Wuhan campaign (Xiaochikou, Huangmei, Guangji, Wuxue, Fuchikou, Tianjiazhen, Banbishan, Qichun, Xishui, Yangxin, Daye, Echeng, Huangshigang, Huanggang, Tuanfeng, Huangpi, Macheng, Huang’an, Yingcheng, Xianning and Chongyang), 8 from the Suixian–Zaoyang and Zaoyang–Yichang campaigns (Suixian, Zaoyang, Xiangyang, Nanzhang, Yicheng, Jingmen, Jingzhou and Dangyang), 4 from the western Hubei campaign (Gong’an, Songzi, Yidu and Changyang), 2 from the 1945 western Henan–northern Hubei campaign (Fancheng and Gucheng) and the Wuhan surrender, with 14 routes (#259–#272). Japanese events rose from 519 to 555 and routes from 258 to 272; the atlas rose from 767 to 803 events and from 437 to 451 routes; Hubei Japanese events rose from 15 to 51. The Wuhan campaign is drawn in three axes (north bank, south bank and the northern Dabie Mountains); the later campaigns are drawn separately and not joined across campaigns. Jiayu, Puqi, Tongshan, Tongcheng, Zhongxiang, Jingshan, Shashi, Yuan’an, Yuyangguan and Duzhenwan lacked two independent sources or duplicated the main line, so they were not hard-recorded or were merged into the text. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-hubei.md. On 21 November 2026, M224 refined the Hunan front: 35 events covering 5 from the first Changsha campaign (Xinqiang River, Yingtian, Miluo River, Pingjiang and Yong’an), 5 from the second (Dayun Mountain, Xinqiang River, Miluo River, Changsha and Zhuzhou), 3 from the third (Xinqiang River, Miluo River and Changsha), 7 from the Changde campaign (Nanxian, Anxiang, Shimen, Lixian, Cili, Taoyuan and Changde), 10 from the Changsha–Hengyang campaign (Xinqiang River, Pingjiang, Yuanjiang, Xiangyin, Yiyang, Liuyang, Zhuzhou, Xiangtan, Youxian and Leiyang), 4 from the western Hunan campaign (Xinning, Dongkou, Wugang and Wuyang) and the Changsha surrender, with 16 routes (#273–#288). Japanese events rose from 555 to 590 and routes from 272 to 288; the atlas rose from 803 to 838 events and from 451 to 467 routes; Hunan Japanese events rose from 15 to 50. The three Changsha campaigns are drawn separately; the Changde campaign in three columns (east, centre and west); the Changsha–Hengyang campaign by northern, eastern, central and southern Hunan; and the western Hunan campaign along the Xinning–Wugang–Dongkou and Dongkou–Wuyang axes, without joining across campaigns. Hanshou, Linli, Ningxiang, Xiangxiang, Liling, Chaling and Anren changed hands repeatedly with conflicting dates, so only the main-line nodes were recorded; Zhijiang was never taken by the Japanese, so no “fall of Zhijiang” is claimed. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-hunan.md. On 21 November 2026, M225 refined the Guangxi front: 25 events covering 10 from the 1939 southern Guangxi campaign (Qinzhou Bay landing, Fangcheng, Qin County, Xiaodong, Gaofeng Pass, Kunlun Pass, Longzhou, Binyang 1940, Wuming 1940 and Shanglin 1940) and 15 from the 1944 Guilin–Liuzhou campaign (Huangshahe, Quanzhou, Wuzhou, Xing’an, Pingnan, Guiping, Lingchuan, Yishan, Xincheng, Hechi, Nandan, Pingxiang, Longzhou 1944, Binyang 1944 and Wuming 1944), with 11 routes (#289–#299). Japanese events rose from 590 to 615 and routes from 288 to 299; the atlas rose from 838 to 863 events and from 467 to 478 routes; Guangxi Japanese events rose from 8 to 33. The 1939 campaign is drawn in three axes (Qinzhou Bay–Nanning–Kunlun Pass/Longzhou); the 1944 campaign by the Hunan–Guangxi railway, the Xi River and the Guangxi–Vietnam highway, without joining across campaigns. In the 1937 frame Qinzhou, Fangcheng and Qin County belonged to Guangdong, so their regional assignment follows the historical frame while the event text retains “Guangxi” for searchability. Existing events for Nanning 1939/1944, Guilin 1944, Liuzhou 1944, the Kunlun Pass counterattack of 18 December 1939 and the Binyang attack of 28 January 1940 were not duplicated; small towns on the pursuit line such as Qianjiang, Liucheng, Rongxian and Luocheng rested on single sources and were not hard-recorded. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-guangxi.md. On 21 November 2026, M226 refined the Yunnan front: 12 events covering 8 from the 1942 invasion of western Yunnan (Zhefang, Mangshi, Tengchong, Ruili, Longchuan, Yingjiang, Lianghe and the Baoshan bombing), 2 from the 1943 border raids (Mengding and Cangyuan) and 2 from the 1944 Japanese defensive posts (Pingjia and Xiangda), with 9 routes (#300–#308); the five 1944 routes are Japanese defensive lines (segmentType: defense). Japanese events rose from 615 to 627 and routes from 299 to 308; the atlas rose from 863 to 875 events and from 478 to 487 routes; Yunnan Japanese events rose from 8 to 20. After the Huitong Bridge was blown up on 5 May 1942 the Japanese never crossed the Salween, so no “fall” events are recorded east of the river. Existing events for Wanding 1942, Longling 1942, the Huitong Bridge 1942 and Songshan/Longling/Tengchong 1944 were not duplicated; Nansan in August 1942 was recorded only by month and was not hard-recorded; the recovery of Mangshi, Zhefang and Wanding in 1944–1945 was a Chinese operation and is not assigned to the Japanese layer. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-yunnan.md. On 22 November 2026, M227 refined the Guizhou, Sichuan and Chongqing front: 17 events covering 5 from the Chongqing bombing (3 May, 4 May, 19 August, 20 August 1940 and the 5 June 1941 tunnel tragedy), 6 from Chengdu and other Sichuan cities (Chengdu 24 July 1940, Chengdu 27 July 1941, Wanxian 4 February 1939, Leshan 19 August 1939, Zigong 12 August 1940 and Luxian 11 September 1939) and 6 from Guizhou (Guiyang 4 February 1939, Liming Pass, Libo, Sandu, Danzhai and Niuchang near Duyun), with 4 routes (#309–#312): Nandan–Mawei–Dushan, Liming Pass–Libo, Sandu–Danzhai–Duyun and Dushan–Duyun (the Japanese withdrawal direction). Japanese events rose from 627 to 644 and routes from 308 to 312; the atlas rose from 875 to 892 events and from 487 to 491 routes; Japanese events in the three regions rose from 3 to 20. The air raids on Chongqing, Chengdu, Wanxian, Leshan, Zigong, Luxian and Guiyang are marked routeEvent:false and no ground advance route is drawn; the Qiannan incident is drawn in three axes, with Dushan–Duyun being the Japanese withdrawal direction rather than an advance. Existing events for Chongqing 18 February 1938, Chengdu 11 June 1939 and Dushan 2 December 1944 were not duplicated; the raids on Chongqing 9/18 August 1940, Fengjie, Wushan, Fuling, Hejiang, Longchang, Nanchuan, Langzhong, Songpan and Yibin were not individually hard-recorded and are left for a later air-raid batch. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-guizhou-sichuan.md. On 22 November 2026, M228 refined the Liaoning front: 20 events covering 12 towns occupied along the South Manchuria and Anfeng railways on 19 September 1931 (Yingkou, Andong, Fushun, Liaoyang, Anshan, Tieling, Benxi, Haicheng, Gaiping, Fuxian, Fengcheng and Kaiyuan), 7 in western Liaoning in 1931–1932 (Xinmin, Xingcheng, Suizhong, Huludao, Yi County, Beizhen and Jinxi) and Xiuyan in eastern Liaoning in 1932, with 10 routes (#313–#322). Japanese events rose from 644 to 664 and routes from 312 to 322; the atlas rose from 892 to 912 events and from 491 to 501 routes; Liaoning Japanese events rose from 4 to 24. The 19 September 1931 occupations are drawn in five branches along the two railways, western Liaoning in three branches, and eastern Liaoning as Haicheng–Xiuyan, without joining across axes. Dalian, Lüshun and Jinzhou (the Kwantung Leased Territory) were not newly occupied in 1931 and are not listed; Siping, Gongzhuling, Changchun and Jilin are left for M229, and Chaoyang, Beipiao, Lingyuan and Jianping for M230. Zhuanghe, Tai’an, Heishan and Changtu were not hard-recorded because their dates are known only by month or changed hands repeatedly. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-liaoning.md. On 22 November 2026, M229 refined the Jilin and Heilongjiang fronts: 24 events covering 12 places in Jilin in 1931\u20131932 (Sipingjie, Shuangcheng, Hailin, Yanji, Longjing, Mudanjiang, Yilan, Jiamusi, Hailun, Ji\u2019an, Linjiang and Tonghua), 6 in Jilin in 1933 (Suifenhe, Suiyang, Dongning, Lishuzhen/Jixi, Mishan and Baoqing), and 6 in Heilongjiang in 1931\u20131932 (Tao\u2019nan, Zhalantun, Yakeshi, Bukettu, Hailar and Manzhouli), with 13 routes (#323\u2013#335). Japanese events rose from 664 to 688 and routes from 322 to 335; the atlas rose from 912 to 936 events and from 501 to 514 routes; Jilin Japanese events rose from 4 to 20 and Heilongjiang from 4 to 8. The eastern Chinese Eastern Railway, the lower Songhua, the Huhai railway, the Tujia direction and the western Chinese Eastern Railway are drawn as separate axes without cross-axis joins; Ji\u2019an, Linjiang and Tonghua are marked routeEvent:false because their approach routes are not documented. Hailar and Manzhouli are assigned to Heilongjiang within its 1932 boundaries; Dalian, L\u00fcshun and Jinzhou (the Kwantung Leased Territory) were not newly occupied in 1931. Jiaohe, Shulan, Dunhua, Ning\u2019an, Fujin, Muling and Suihua were not hard-recorded because of single sources or conflicting dates. All routes are schematic; sources and pending items are listed in docs/research/units/anti-japanese-war-jilin-heilongjiang.md.

description.zh: 自 1931 年九一八事变起，日本关东军及后续侵华部队在中国东北、华北、华中、华南的进攻方向，路线为示意简化。
description.en: Advance directions of the Japanese Kwantung Army and subsequent invasion forces in Northeast, North, Central, and South China from 1931; routes are simplified.

description.zh: 国民政府及其战时政治、外交、经济与军事决策；军事行动路线已按部队拆分到国民党军、集团军、八路军、盟军等实体。
description.en: The Nationalist government and its wartime political, diplomatic, economic, and military decisions; military routes have been reassigned to the KMT, group-army, Eighth Route Army, and Allied layers.

description.zh: 国际联盟、九国公约会议等多边组织与会议的调查、调处与决议；行为主体是国际组织或会议，不是中国政府。
description.en: Investigations, mediation, and resolutions by the League of Nations, the Nine-Power Conference, and other multilateral bodies; the actor is the international organization or conference, not the Chinese government.

description.zh: 学生、知识分子、社会团体、民众武装、难民与战时救援；不包含政府决策与军队作战。
description.en: Students, intellectuals, civic groups, people’s armed forces, refugees, and wartime relief; government decisions and military operations are excluded.

name.en: Allied Forces and Chinese Expeditionary Force

description.zh: 太平洋战争爆发后，中国与美、英等盟国在中缅印战区协同作战；路线表现中国远征军入缅、撤退与缅北反攻。
description.en: After the Pacific War began, China fought alongside the United States, Britain, and other Allies in the China-Burma-India theater; routes show the Chinese Expeditionary Force’s entry into Burma, retreat, and the northern Burma counteroffensive.

description.zh: 国民革命军正面战场部队与作战序列；路线为示意简化，待史料校订。
description.en: National Revolutionary Army frontline units and order of battle; routes are simplified and await historical review.

description.zh: 国民革命军第八路军及其华北敌后根据地；路线为示意简化，待史料校订。
description.en: The Eighth Route Army and its base areas in North China; routes are simplified and await historical review.

description.zh: 国民革命军陆军新编第四军及其华中敌后根据地；路线为示意简化，待史料校订。
description.en: The New Fourth Army and its base areas in Central China; routes are simplified and await historical review.

description.zh: 东江纵队、琼崖纵队等华南抗日武装；路线为示意简化，待史料校订。
description.en: South China anti-Japanese forces including the Dongjiang and Qiongya columns; routes are simplified and await historical review.

description.zh: 国民革命军集团军层级部队与作战序列；路线为示意简化，待史料校订。
description.en: National Revolutionary Army group armies and their order of battle; routes are simplified and await historical review.

description.zh: 1931—1945 年中华民国名义省界示意，只描边不填充；边界为手工绘制，非精确勘界。
description.en: Schematic ROC provincial boundaries, 1931–1945. Outline only; hand-drawn, not survey-grade.
